entries.title: C0120 primary-source model: draft scope correction
entries.statement: Source-scope audit draft, awaiting independent review: the cited arXiv:0810.4221v2 Section 8 concerns M_n, the maximum sum of iid standard Gaussian weights over n-vertex up-right paths from the origin in Z^2 with a free endpoint. Its logarithmic variance bound is for M_n. The intake replacement by an arbitrary-dimensional log partition function needs a separate source. A power improvement for this precise M_n is not proved here; current openness is UNKNOWN.
assumptions: Historical citation arXiv:0810.4221v2; not a current-openness certification

entries.title: Polynomial chaos cutoff for Gaussian path variance: draft reduction
entries.statement: Draft conditional reduction, not an independently certified theorem: let v_nk be the degree-k Gaussian chaos variance of the centered source-model M_n. The path-indicator gradient has squared norm n almost surely, giving sum k v_nk=n. Hence Var(M_n)<=sum_{k<=K}v_nk+n/(K+1). A bound sum_{k<=ceil(n^delta)}v_nk<=C n^(1-delta), for fixed 0<delta<1 uniformly in n, would give a power variance improvement. This low-chaos-mass input remains unproved.

entries.title: Independent Gaussian layer averages: draft exact decomposition
entries.statement: Draft lemma awaiting independent review: in the source model let A_t be the mean weight of the t+1 vertices on x+y=t, and R_v=g_v-A_t on that layer. Joint Gaussianity and zero cross covariance make the entire vector of A_t independent of the entire R vector. Every path visits one vertex per layer, so M_n(g)=sum_t A_t+M_n(R) and Var(M_n)=H_n+Var(M_n(R)), with H_n=sum_{j=1}^n 1/j. Residual weights within each layer are correlated; the split supplies no residual upper bound.
assumptions: n vertices starting at the origin and moving up/right

entries.title: Fixed-degree suppression alone: draft spectral counterexample
entries.statement: Draft counterexample awaiting independent review: for k_n=ceil(log n), normalized probabilists Hermite polynomial H_k and G~N(0,1), F_n=sqrt(n/k_n) H_k_n(G) has variance n/k_n and Gaussian Dirichlet energy n. Every fixed chaos degree eventually vanishes, and normalized gradient covariance tends to zero at every fixed positive Ornstein-Uhlenbeck time, yet no fixed power variance bound follows. This example is not a convex or Lipschitz polymer maximum.
assumptions: General Gaussian Sobolev functions; not the source lattice class

entries.title: Qualitative chaos without a power gain: draft Gaussian fan control
entries.statement: Draft counterexample awaiting independent review: on the graph with a common root and n disjoint branches of n-1 vertices with iid standard Gaussian weights, the maximum n-vertex path sum is convex and sqrt(n)-Lipschitz, with path-indicator gradient of squared norm n. It has normalized expected overlap tending to zero at Ornstein-Uhlenbeck time u_n=16 log(log n)/log n, yet Var(M_n)>=c n/log n for all sufficiently large n and some c>0. Thus these structural facts alone do not yield a power bound. The growing-degree fan is not Z^2; fixed lattice geometry may provide the missing quantitative premise.
assumptions: n large enough that u_n>0 and the Mills-bound quantile b_n>=1
A different fan graph for each n; root degree n
Not a counterexample to C0120 on Z^2

relations.rationale: The spectral identity uses the Gaussian path maximum and its path-indicator gradient specified by the source-model concept.
The layer sizes t+1 and exactly one visited vertex per layer come from this two-dimensional up-right source model.

Both give variance lower bounds of logarithmic rather than fixed-power scale while displaying qualitative Gaussian decorrelation; the fan also preserves convexity and a bounded path-indicator gradient.
The fan control shows why a qualitative overlap statement cannot supply the quantitative polynomial cutoff required by the reduction; it does not disprove that cutoff for the lattice model.
